Introduction

Starting a Personal Services Agency (PSA) in Indiana enables you to provide non-medical home care services including personal care, homemaker, and companion services. Indiana’s growing senior population creates strong demand.

The IN Department of Health (IDOH) — Division of Home & Community-Based Care licenses and regulates Personal Services Agencies under Indiana Administrative Code.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Indiana’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Indiana’s Regulations

IDOH licenses PSAs under specific regulations. Key requirements:

  • State licensing through IDOH Division of Home & Community-Based Care
  • Background checks for all direct care staff
  • Training requirements per Indiana regulations
  • Service documentation and record-keeping standards

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker services, companion care, respite care, and transportation assistance.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

  • Register with the IN Secretary of State
  • Apply for PSA license through IDOH
  • Obtain required insurance and bonding
  • Complete Medicaid provider enrollment if applicable

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Indiana financial benchmarks:

  • Private pay rates: $20 to $28 per hour
  • Medicaid rates: $16 to $22 per hour
  • Break-even timeline: 12 to 18 months

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, technology systems, scheduling software, and quality monitoring tools.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Indiana requires background checks and competency training for all direct care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop comprehensive operational policies meeting IDOH requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Build referral networks with healthcare providers, Area Agencies on Aging, and community organizations.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain license, training records, and quality improvement programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

 

How long does PSA licensing take?

Typically 60 to 90 days for complete applications.

What services can a PSA provide?

Non-medical personal care, homemaker, companion, and related support services.
